def _check_base_locator(verb, required, source_url, source_page, source_line, source_clause):

    --first-form (T-028): the named flags present, a page or a clause, no blank locator part, an
    http(s) URL with a host and no whitespace, a line of 1 or more. Returns the trimmed URL, page and
    clause (a blank locator part is no locator: trimmed, then refused by name)."""
    source_url, source_page, source_clause = ((v.strip() if isinstance(v, str) else v)
                                              for v in (source_url, source_page, source_clause))
    missing = [f for f, v in required if not (v.strip() if isinstance(v, str) else v)]

              usage_type: str = None):

                    source used it is read; `instrument` needs the source to belong to the
                    regulatory stratum, derived from the tier ladder);
      base          --alias T --language XX --jurisdiction YY --source-url U
                    (--source-page P | --source-clause C) [--source-line N]

                    and created_by_session the judge (no rationale column, T-026);

    sanctioned path. Aliases are a reading aid, never evidence (catalogue-plan-v2 section
    3.9). NOTHING IS TYPED THAT THE MACHINE CAN READ (CLAUDE.md rule 8): on the observation
    route the alias IS the observation's surface form, its language the observation's (in
    term_aliases' own letter case, measured by _alias_language) and its jurisdiction the
    source's; the operator chooses only the alias type, from the column's CHECK. The base
    route has no observation to read, so it names them, and the pair must be one
    lang_jur_map holds.

    owner_supplied or unrecorded, with no observation or this one) PROMOTES that row in place

    whose quote is not in a file saved for its source (unless VERBATIM-EXEMPT); `instrument` for a

    that is not http(s)://host with no whitespace, a pair lang_jur_map lacks, or an attestation
    outside instrument|other_source; a seed route with a locator or an attestation, a seed
    that is an attestation, `model_seed`, or `owner_supplied` with no ledger heading naming

                          f"read in an instrument or another source takes the base route.")

                          f"ledger entries; it must be exactly one. Nothing was written.")

                          "as a form any more: rename-term keeps the former label in term_label_picks. "
                          "A phrase a source uses is a live alias.")
        if alias_type == "TRANSLATION":

                          "English one. A phrase a source uses is its own jurisdiction's term "
                          "(R11, no back-translation): record it as SYNONYM, NARROWER or "

        if alias_type == "DOMAIN":

        if usage_type is not None:
            dbcore.check_declared(conn, "term_aliases", "usage_type", usage_type, "add-alias --usage-type")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "term_aliases", "attestation", attestation or seed,
                              "add-alias --attestation/--seed")
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "terms", "term_id", term_id):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id!r}: no such term.")

                dry_run: bool = False, *, from_form: int = None, judge: str = None):

    `amend-term` refused canonical_en since 2026-09-25 ("a vocabulary decision with
    callers, not a wording fix"), and no other verb could change it, so an answer-shaped
    or mis-chosen name was permanent (critique F5; plan section 1.2 item 6: the held ADA
    text says "turning space" and not "turning circle"). This is that vocabulary
    decision, with its warrant required, exactly one of:

      --from-form F         an ATTESTED member form of THIS term (instrument or other_source,
                            not NARROWER or BROADER) whose text is the new label: the stored
                            pick of the name shown when several English instruments name the
                            concept differently (T-028; OD-38, owner 2026-11-12: "First recorded,
                            until a named judge picks; the pick is recorded with its reason");
      --from-observation N  the new name comes from a phrase a source USES, in the
                            source's own language (owner E1, 2026-11-06: a concept first
                            met outside English is named by that phrase), whose latest adjudication names
                            THIS term, whose surface form
                            contains the new name (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept by the owner
                            on 2026-10-09: names come from observed phrases);
      --ruling-quote "..."  or from the owner's own words, quoted verbatim and found
                            exactly once in references/project-standards.md, containing
                            the new name.
    Every route names its --judge (who picked) beside the --reason (OD-38).

    Nothing else moves: parameters, adjudications and extractions point at term_id, so the
    name is reached, never copied (rule 5). The label is not a form (OD-03), so the former
    label is NOT written into term_aliases and no AMENDED trailer is appended to scope_note
    (the owner's schema-shape statement of 2026-11-06: a correction appended to a note is a fact
    in the wrong cell): one term_label_picks row holds the former label, the route's one pointer,
    the judge and the reason. No other term may hold the new name, as a label or as an attested
    English form (_name_holder); a seed never refuses (E4).

    REFUSES: no judge; neither or several warrants; a value-bearing name (_VALUE_BEARING, as
    add-term); a quote not exactly once in the ledger or not containing the name; an observation
    whose latest adjudication does not name this term, or that does not contain the name; a form
    that is not an attested member form of this term or whose text is not the name; a name another
    term holds.
    """
    new = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    if not new:
        raise Refusal("rename-term: --canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, term_id)
    judge = (judge or "").strip()
    if not judge:
        raise Refusal("rename-term: --judge is required: who picked this label (OD-38, owner 2026-11-12: "
                      "the pick is recorded with its reason, and a pick names its judge). Nothing was written.")
    if (from_observation is not None) + bool((ruling_quote or "").strip()) + (from_form is not None) != 1:
        raise Refusal(
            "rename-term: give exactly one warrant for the new name -- --from-form F (an attested "
            "form of this term), --from-observation N (a phrase an admitted source uses) or "
            "--ruling-quote '<the owner's words>' (found once in references/project-standards.md). "
            "A name with no warrant is a name typed by hand, which the 2026-09-09 rule forbids.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(new)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"rename-term: {new!r} carries a number, a comparator or a min/max word "
            f"({vb.group(0)!r}), so it "
            f"states a determination in its own name -- the item-layer defect "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 section 1.1). Name the quantity, never its value.")
    if ruling_quote:
        dbcore.require_ledger_quote_once(ruling_quote, "rename-term: the --ruling-quote",
                                         "That ties this rename to one ruling.")
        if new.lower() not in dbcore.normalise_quote_text(ruling_quote).lower():
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: the quoted ruling does not contain {new!r}; the "
                          f"words that authorise a name must say it.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        term = conn.execute("SELECT term_id, canonical_en FROM terms "
                            "WHERE term_id = ?", (term_id,)).fetchone()
        if term is None:
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {term_id!r}: no such term.")
        old = term["canonical_en"]
        if old == new:
            return {"term_id": term_id, "changed": False, "dry_run": dry_run}
        for clash in _name_holder(conn, new, "EN", exclude_term=term_id)["clashes"]:
            if clash["kind"] == "label":
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {new!r} is already the name of {clash['term_id']}. "
                              f"Two terms with one name are one concept twice; that is a merge, "
                              f"not a rename. Nothing was written.")
            raise Refusal(f"rename-term: {new!r} is an alias ({clash['detail']}, form {clash['form_id']}) of "
                          f"{clash['term_id']}, attested. A name another term answers to would make "
                          f"one phrase point at two concepts. Nothing was written.")
        if from_form is not None:
            form = conn.execute("SELECT form_id, alias, alias_type, attestation FROM term_aliases "
                                "WHERE form_id = ? AND term_id = ?", (from_form, term_id)).fetchone()
            if (form is None or form["attestation"] not in dbcore.ATTESTED_FORMS
                    or form["alias_type"] in ("NARROWER", "BROADER")):
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: form {from_form} is not an attested member form of {term_id} "
                              f"(instrument or other_source, not NARROWER or BROADER): a label is picked from "
                              f"the forms a source uses for this concept. Nothing was written.")
            if form["alias"] != new:
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: form {from_form} reads {form['alias']!r}, not {new!r}: a label "
                              f"picked from a form is that form's text. Nothing was written.")
        elif from_observation is not None:
            obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, ref_id, surface_form, language "
                               "FROM observed_terms WHERE observation_id = ?",
                               (from_observation,)).fetchone()
            if obs is None:
                raise Refusal(f"rename-term: observation {from_observation}: no such "
                              f"observed term.")
            if not _names_term(conn, from_observation, term_id):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"{_not_named_msg(conn, 'rename-term', from_observation, term_id)} "
                    f"If the source's phrase does name THIS concept, judge it: db.py adjudicate-term "
                    f"--observation-id {from_observation} --outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {term_id} "
                    f"--rationale ... --session ... (a later adjudication is the standing one), then rename "
                    f"from it. Nothing was written.")
            if not _retrieval_log().phrase_in_quote(new, obs["surface_form"]):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"rename-term: {new!r} is not in the observed phrase "
                    f"{obs['surface_form']!r}. A name taken from a source is the source's "
                    f"words. Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        pick = {"term_id": term_id, "former_label": old, "form_id": from_form,
                "observation_id": from_observation,
                "ruling_quote": ruling_quote.strip() if ruling_quote else None,
                "judge": judge, "reason": reason}
        pick.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_label_picks", session))
        pick_id = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_label_picks ({','.join(pick)}) "
                               f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(pick))})", list(pick.values())).lastrowid
        sets = {"canonical_en": new}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "terms", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE terms SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE term_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [term_id])
        return {"term_id": term_id, "was": old, "now": new, "pick_id": pick_id, "judge": judge,
                "changed": True, "dry_run": dry_run}

                "dry_run": dry_run}


def retire_term_relation(relation_id: int, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Retire one `term_relations` row in place (OD-29): the three retired_* columns, never an UPDATE of the rest.

    Refuses: no such relation; one already retired (it is never revived: write a new row); a blank reason."""
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, "retire-term-relation",
                                   why="Say why the terms are no longer so related.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT relation_id, retired_at FROM term_relations WHERE relation_id=?",
                           (relation_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-term-relation: relation {relation_id}: no such relation. Nothing was written.")
        if row["retired_at"] is not None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-term-relation: relation {relation_id} was retired at {row['retired_at']}. A "
                          f"retired relation is not revived; write a new one with add-term-relation. Nothing "
                          f"was written.")
        conn.execute("UPDATE term_relations SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=? "
                     "WHERE relation_id=?",
                     [dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session), reason, relation_id])
        return {"relation_id": relation_id, "retired": True, "dry_run": dry_run}


def element_parameters(element: str):
    """Read-only (T-029; read by T-033 and render): an element term's parameters and its provisions.

    The live `element has parameter` and `element has provision` rows from the element, each with the term it
    points at, that term's parameter if it has one (`base_parameters.term_id`, looked up and never copied), the
    reason and the warrant pointer. A provision whose term also carries a parameter is printed as it is: the
    provision is not a parameter (OD-56), and the reader does not hide the contradiction."""
    with connect(readonly=True) as conn:
        el = conn.execute("SELECT term_id, canonical_en FROM terms WHERE term_id=?", (element,)).fetchone()
        if el is None:
            raise Refusal(f"element-parameters: --element {element!r}: no such term. Read the terms with "
                          f"`python3 scripts/db.py next-id --entity terms` for the next id, or query terms.")
        out = {"element": {"term_id": el["term_id"], "label": el["canonical_en"]}}
        for key, kind in (("parameters", "element has parameter"), ("provisions", "element has provision")):
            out[key] = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(
                "SELECT r.relation_id, r.to_term_id AS term_id, t.canonical_en AS label, p.parameter_id, "
                "p.status AS parameter_status, r.reason, r.observation_id, r.extraction_id, r.adjudication_id, "
                "r.created_by_session, r.created_at "
                "FROM term_relations r JOIN terms t ON t.term_id = r.to_term_id "
                "LEFT JOIN base_parameters p ON p.term_id = r.to_term_id "
                "WHERE r.from_term_id=? AND r.kind=? AND r.retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY r.relation_id",
                (element, kind))]
        return out

-- SCHEMA migration -- a compensating migration for 147_term_relations (T-029; 147 is committed and is not edited).
-- Tooling, no research rows. The table holds no rows when this runs, and the copy below carries any it holds.
-- Rebuilt by create, copy, drop, rename, because SQLite cannot change a CHECK in place.
--
-- WHAT CHANGES, each the repair of a defect the adversarial pass found in 147:
--  1. THE RETIREMENT CHECK. 147's form `length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0` is NULL when the reason is NULL, and a
--     CHECK that evaluates to NULL passes, so a row retired with a session and no reason was accepted. The three cells
--     now follow the siblings' form (search_admissions, connections: `(a IS NULL) = (b IS NULL)`), and a non-blank guard
--     that cannot be NULL-passed (the equalities make the other two cells non-NULL whenever retired_at is).
--  2. `element has provision` takes no adjudication warrant. OD-56 names the source statements that say an element
--     should carry a provision: observation rows and extraction rows. T-029's file names the same two.
--  3. `reason` is nullable (its blank is still refused). T-029's file names a warrant and no reason cell; T-129's design
--     (section A6) sets a `distinct` row's reason to the rationale text, which its warrant adjudication already holds.
--     Whether the cell survives is a design question recorded in the commit; until it is answered the cell may be empty.
--  4. `distinct` is stored with the lower term id first, compared by the number after the id's hyphen (TERM-999 is below
--     TERM-1000), the text only breaking a tie. The writer derives the same key from the id's own form.
-- Everything else is 147's, unchanged: the kinds, the warrant (exactly one pointer), and the one live row per unordered
-- pair per kind.

CREATE TABLE _148_term_relations (
    relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    from_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    kind                TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (kind IN ('broader', 'part of', 'element has parameter', 'element has provision',
                                        'adjacent', 'distinct')),
    to_term_id          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    reason              TEXT CHECK (reason IS NULL OR length(trim(reason)) > 0),
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    extraction_id       INTEGER REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
    adjudication_id     INTEGER REFERENCES term_adjudications(adjudication_id),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    CHECK (from_term_id <> to_term_id),
    CHECK ((observation_id IS NOT NULL) + (extraction_id IS NOT NULL) + (adjudication_id IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK (kind <> 'element has provision' OR adjudication_id IS NULL),
    CHECK (kind <> 'distinct'
           OR CAST(substr(from_term_id, instr(from_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
              < CAST(substr(to_term_id, instr(to_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
           OR (CAST(substr(from_term_id, instr(from_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
               = CAST(substr(to_term_id, instr(to_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
               AND from_term_id < to_term_id)),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL)),
    CHECK (retired_at IS NULL OR (length(trim(retired_at)) > 0 AND length(trim(retired_by_session)) > 0
                                  AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0))
);

                                 adjudication_id, created_at, created_by_session, retired_at, retired_by_session,
                                 retirement_reason)
SELECT relation_id, from_term_id, kind, to_term_id, reason, observation_id, extraction_id, adjudication_id,
       created_at, created_by_session, retired_at, retired_by_session, retirement_reason
  FROM term_relations;

-- 149_base_units.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-030; no data rows beyond the seed of the unit table). Units, and the exact factor that relates
-- the units of one quantity kind, are rows.
--
-- WHY. The engine owned one hard-coded family (the gradient notations `%` and `rise:run ratio`), so a parameter whose
-- sources state the same length in millimetres, centimetres and metres declined to compose ("stated in different units"),
-- and a length family could be added only by editing the engine (GAP-072, GAP-094). OR-10 (owner, 2026-10-29): the engine
-- may compose across exact length units and present both. OD-24 (delegated resolution 2026-11-12): units belong to the
-- quantity kinds of T-020. OD-22 and OD-42 (delegated resolutions 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13): a conversion between metric
-- prefixes is shown exactly; a conversion between inch-foot and metric is shown at the nearest quarter inch or 5 mm that
-- does not fall on the wrong side of the source's bound; the stored bound stays exact.
--
-- WHAT. base_units: one row per unit as a source writes it in claimed_unit, the kind it measures (a row of
-- base_quantity_kinds, T-020), and its factor as two integers, so the conversion is exact in Fraction and never a float:
-- one of this unit is factor_numerator / factor_denominator of the kind's CANONICAL unit. The canonical unit of a kind is
-- the one unit whose factor is 1 (the unique index below allows at most one; a kind with none cannot compose and the
-- reader says so). figure_form says how a figure of the unit is written: `number`, or `ratio` (written a:b, the figure
-- being a divided by b, so `1:12` under `rise:run ratio` is 100/12 percent). system says which measuring system a length
-- unit belongs to, because the shown figure is rounded to the owner's increment only when the shown unit's system is not
-- the system the source stated it in; NULL for a unit that has no such system. The increments themselves (5 mm; a quarter
-- inch) are the owner's ruling and live once, in dbcore.SHOWN_STEPS, beside the converter that applies them.
--
-- SEED. Every factor is a definition, not a measurement: the international inch is 25.4 mm exactly (1959) and the foot is
-- twelve inches, so 127/5 and 1524/5 millimetres. The two gradient notations are the pair NOTATION_FAMILIES held in
-- dbcore (owner ruling 2026-09-17, "Present both"); percent is canonical. `degrees` is NOT seeded: it is the arctangent
-- of the gradient, not a rescaling, so no exact factor relates it to percent. No force, time or other unit is seeded:
-- a unit is added when a parameter of its kind needs a conversion, by a migration (no verb writes this table).
--
-- WHAT READS IT. dbcore.load_units and the functions built on it (to_canonical, from_canonical, bound_on_scale,
-- figure_refusal), read by assess_cell.compose_value and by db.py add-extraction / amend-extraction (through figure_refusal
-- and the reformat rule).

CREATE TABLE base_units (
    unit                TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(trim(unit)) > 0 AND unit = trim(unit)),
    kind_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_quantity_kinds(kind_id),
    factor_numerator    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (factor_numerator > 0),
    factor_denominator  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (factor_denominator > 0),
    figure_form         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (figure_form IN ('number', 'ratio')),
    system              TEXT CHECK (system IS NULL OR system IN ('metric', 'inch-foot')),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT
);

p='scripts/dbcore.py'

#: quantity kind it measures (`base_quantity_kinds`, T-020) and its factor to the kind's CANONICAL unit (the unit whose
#: factor is 1) as two integers, so every conversion is exact in Fraction and never a float. A unit is added by a row, not by
#: an edit here. This replaces `NOTATION_FAMILIES` (owner ruling 2026-09-17, "Present both -- don't choose between ratio or
#: percentage", extended to exact length units by OR-10, 2026-10-29): the gradient notations are two rows of the kind
#: `gradient`, and the lengths are rows of the kind `length`.
#:
#: A KIND IS NOT A GUESS ABOUT TWO NOTATIONS. Two units of one kind denote one quantity exactly (a metre is 1000 millimetres;
#: `1:12` is 100/12 percent); units of different kinds never convert (millimetres and percent, or a unit with no row, stay
#: apart and the engine refuses to compose them). `degrees` has no row: it is the ARCTANGENT of the gradient, not a
#: rescaling, so no exact factor relates it to percent.
#:
#: THE ROUNDING RULE, declared once, here (the owner's rulings, OD-22 and OD-42 in references/project-standards.md, "Delegated
#: resolution 2026-11-12 -- OD-22" and "Delegated resolution 2026-11-13 -- OD-42"; both resolved under delegation, the
#: owner's increment being OR-10): a figure shown in a unit of the SAME system as the unit the source stated (a change of
#: metric prefix) keeps the source's digits and is exact. A figure shown in a unit of the OTHER system (inch-foot to metric)
#: is shown at the nearest increment of the shown unit's system that does not fall on the wrong side of the source's
#: bound: a minimum is never shown below it, a maximum never above it; the stored bound stays exact. The increment is the
#: owner's, in the kind's canonical unit (5 mm; a quarter inch is 127/20 mm), keyed by (kind, system). A JUDGED RULE, not a
#: derived one, so it is a typed constant (the NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS precedent below); a test holds its keys inside the
#: live rows (a renamed kind or system cannot silently disarm it).
SHOWN_STEPS = {("length", "metric"): Fraction(5), ("length", "inch-foot"): Fraction(127, 20)}
_RATIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*:\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*$")

UnitRow = namedtuple("UnitRow", "unit kind factor figure_form system")

    members are the rows sharing its `kind` -- there is no second list. Raises sqlite3.OperationalError when the table
    is missing: a database without it cannot read a unit, and saying nothing would read every unit as standing alone."""
    return {r[0]: UnitRow(r[0], r[1], Fraction(r[2], r[3]), r[4], r[5]) for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT unit, kind_id, factor_numerator, factor_denominator, figure_form, system FROM base_units "
        "ORDER BY CAST(factor_numerator AS REAL) / factor_denominator, unit")}

    """The quantity kind a stated unit measures, or None if it has no row and so stands alone."""
    row = load_units(conn).get((unit or "").strip())
    return row.kind if row else None


def kind_members(conn, kind):
    """The units of a kind, canonical first."""
    return [u for u, r in load_units(conn).items() if r.kind == kind]


def canonical_unit(conn, kind):
    """The unit whose factor is 1 (the unique index allows one). A kind with none cannot be composed, and falling
    through would read a number as if it were already on a scale: refused."""
    for u, r in load_units(conn).items():

        "or remove the kind's units. Falling through would read the number as if it were already canonical." % (kind,))
